title: 2nd Stopping Place 5th Truth The Unity Of Name And Act And The All Encompassing Nature Of Elements And Species

questions.question: What is said about the basic materials of creation and where they are found?
questions.answer: They are spread across the whole earth.

questions.question: What is said about each kind of created thing that shows a sign of oneness?
questions.answer: Each kind is found widely over the earth in a united way.

questions.question: What does the spread of the elements and species show clearly?
questions.answer: It shows they all belong to one Creator.

questions.question: How are the elements described in relation to that one Creator?
questions.answer: They are like strong servants under His command.

questions.question: How are the species and their many individual members described?
questions.answer: They are like orderly soldiers serving under one ruler.

questions.question: What does this comparison to servants and soldiers help us understand?
questions.answer: It helps us understand that one powerful Lord controls them all.

questions.question: Why does the passage connect wide spread across the earth with unity instead of many owners?
questions.answer: Because things that work together in the same way across the earth point to one owner, not many separate ones.

questions.question: What quality of the Creator is especially highlighted by commanding huge elements and many species?
questions.answer: His unique power and unmatched authority.

questions.question: Does the passage give a long full proof here or only a short reminder?
questions.answer: It gives only a short reminder.

questions.question: After mentioning this truth, what does the passage say the traveler does?
questions.answer: He prepares to speak from the strong faith and joy he gained from the five truths.

questions.question: What fills the whole earth according to the passage?
questions.answer: The elements that make up created things fill the earth.

questions.question: What is special about the different kinds of living or created things mentioned here?
questions.answer: They carry signs that point to oneness and are spread all over the earth.

questions.question: When the passage says these species almost take over the earth, what idea is it giving?
questions.answer: It means they are found everywhere in a broad and powerful way.

questions.question: What conclusion is drawn from the earthwide spread of elements and species?
questions.answer: They must come from one being and belong to Him.

questions.question: What two relationships do these things have to that one being?
questions.answer: They are His products and also His servants.

questions.question: What does calling the elements obedient teach us about them?
questions.answer: They do not act on their own but follow Allah’s command.

questions.question: What does calling the species disciplined soldiers teach us about creation?
questions.answer: It shows there is order, control, and one commander over them.

questions.question: Which is a better summary of the main point: many powers are competing, or one power is ruling?
questions.answer: One power is ruling.

questions.question: What reason is given for not explaining this truth in detail here?
questions.answer: It has already been explained in other parts of the Risale-i Nur.

questions.question: According to the passage, what covers the earth from among the materials of creation?
questions.answer: The basic elements of creation cover the earth.

questions.question: What is true of each species that points to unity?
questions.answer: Each one is spread throughout the earth as a single kind.

questions.question: How does the passage move from observation to belief?
questions.answer: It looks at the worldwide spread of things and concludes that one Creator made and owns them.

questions.question: What does the word “property” mean in this passage?
questions.answer: It means these things belong to one Lord.

questions.question: What image is used for the mighty elements?
questions.answer: They are pictured as servants that obey.

questions.question: What image is used for species spread around the world?
questions.answer: They are pictured as trained soldiers.

questions.question: What do both images have in common?
questions.answer: Both show obedience, order, and one leader.

questions.question: What feeling does the traveler have after seeing the five truths?
questions.answer: He feels strong faith and happiness in Allah’s oneness.

questions.question: What does he do because of those feelings?
questions.answer: He speaks to his own heart.

questions.question: What part of creation is called the substance and material of created things?
questions.answer: The elements are called the material of creation.

questions.question: How far do these elements reach?
questions.answer: They reach across the whole earth.

questions.question: What is said about the species that carry signs of unity?
questions.answer: They are spread over the earth in a united way.

questions.question: If many species are found all over the world in an ordered way, what does that suggest?
questions.answer: It suggests one Maker arranged and owns them.

questions.question: What does the passage say about the elements together with all they include?
questions.answer: They are all the work and possession of one being.

questions.question: What does the passage say about the species together with their members?
questions.answer: They too are the work and possession of that same one being.

questions.question: Which two traits of that one being are directly emphasized?
questions.answer: His uniqueness and His great power.

questions.question: How does the passage describe the Creator’s rule over huge natural forces?
questions.answer: He uses them like obedient workers under His command.

questions.question: How does the passage describe His rule over the many kinds of created beings on earth?
questions.answer: He uses them like well-trained soldiers.

questions.question: What writing choice appears at the end of this paragraph?
questions.answer: The explanation is kept brief because the matter was already explained elsewhere.

questions.question: What does the passage first ask us to notice about the elements?
questions.answer: That they are present throughout the earth.

questions.question: What does it ask us to notice about the different species?
questions.answer: That each kind is spread widely across the earth and shows a sign of oneness.

questions.question: Why is the spread of species important in the argument?
questions.answer: Because their shared pattern across the earth points to one source.

questions.question: What is the main belief proved by these signs?
questions.answer: That one Creator made, owns, and governs them all.

questions.question: How does the passage describe the connection between creation and this one Creator?
questions.answer: Creation is His making and serves under Him.

questions.question: What can a 5th-grade student learn from the picture of obedient servants?
questions.answer: Even very great forces are under Allah’s control.

questions.question: What can a 5th-grade student learn from the picture of disciplined soldiers?
questions.answer: Living things are arranged with order and do not exist by accident.

questions.question: What kind of proof is this passage using most: a proof from guessing or a proof from what is seen?
questions.answer: It uses proof from what is seen in the world.

questions.question: After these truths, what two feelings are especially mentioned in the traveler?
questions.answer: Full faith and joy in Allah’s oneness.

questions.question: Who does the traveler speak to next?
questions.answer: He speaks to his own heart.

questions.question: What does the passage say about how widely the elements of creation are found?
questions.answer: They are found over the entire earth.

questions.question: What does the passage say about the created kinds that bear signs of unity?
questions.answer: They are spread across the earth as single, recognizable kinds.

questions.question: What lesson is drawn from both the elements and the species being so widespread?
questions.answer: They all come from one owner and maker.

questions.question: What does the phrase “self-evident” show about this lesson?
questions.answer: It shows the proof is very clear and easy to recognize.

questions.question: Are the elements and species described as independent rulers or as those under command?
questions.answer: They are described as those under command.

questions.question: In the passage, what role do the mighty elements play under the Creator?
questions.answer: They act like obedient servants.

questions.question: In the passage, what role do the species spread around the world play under the Creator?
questions.answer: They act like organized soldiers.

questions.question: What does this tell us about the order of the world?
questions.answer: The world is ruled with discipline and unity.

questions.question: Why does the passage stop with a short indication instead of a long explanation?
questions.answer: Because this truth had already been established elsewhere.

questions.question: What does the traveler do after gathering witness from the five truths?
questions.answer: He sums up what he saw and speaks out of faith and happiness about Divine unity.
